sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability
sections.content: Briefly revisit the idea of 'Information Updating'. Define P(A|B) as the probability of A given that B has already occurred, visualized as narrowing our focus from the whole sample space to the subset B.
sections.example: A deck of cards: If you know the card is Red (Subset B), what is the probability it is a Heart (A)?

sections.title: The Concept of Independence
sections.content: Define independence as: Knowing that B happened gives zero new info about A. Mathematically: P(A|B) = P(A), or P(A ∩ B) = P(A) * P(B). Use a Venn diagram showing two distinct, non-overlapping constraints.
sections.example: Flipping a coin (A) and rolling a die (B). The outcome of the coin flip does not change the probability of rolling a 6.

sections.title: Introducing Bayes' Theorem
sections.content: Present the theorem as an 'Inversion Formula'. Explain that we often know P(Evidence|Hypothesis) but want to find P(Hypothesis|Evidence). Use a flow diagram: Prior -> Likelihood -> Evidence -> Posterior.
sections.example: A 'Sniffer Dog' (Device) detection scenario: If the dog barks (Evidence), how likely is there truly a treat in the bag (Hypothesis)?

sections.title: The Core Calculation: Bayes' Formula
sections.content: Walk through the formula P(H|E) = [P(E|H) * P(H)] / P(E). Break down P(E) into the Law of Total Probability: P(E|H)P(H) + P(E|not H)P(not H). Use a tree diagram to visualize the branching paths.
sections.example: Calculating the accuracy of a medical test: Given a positive result, what is the actual probability of having the condition, accounting for false positives?

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Conclude by contrasting the two concepts: Independence simplifies probability (multiplication), while Bayes' Theorem updates probability based on new evidence. Emphasize that Bayes is the foundation of modern machine learning.
sections.example: Email Spam Filters: 'Independence' helps us simplify naive Bayes models, while the 'Theorem' updates the probability that an incoming email is 'Spam' based on keywords.

storyboard.title: The Concept of Independence
lecture_lines: Independence means B provides no info about A.
Flipping coins and dice are independent events.
animations: Display two independent events A and B separately in #FFFFFF.
Show the probability product rule: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B).
Use color #00FF00 to highlight that P(A|B) equals P(A).

storyboard.title: Introducing Bayes' Theorem
lecture_lines: We use evidence to find our hypothesis.
Prior, Likelihood, Evidence, Posterior form the cycle.
A sniffer dog detects a hidden treat.
We update our belief after evidence appears.

Highlight P(B|A) in color #FF0000 on the left side.
Highlight P(A|B) in color #0000FF on the right side.

storyboard.title: The Core Calculation: Bayes' Formula
lecture_lines: Total probability defines our denominator P(E).
A tree diagram visualizes these branching paths.
Medical tests must account for false positives.

Use color #FF8000 to frame the Numerator component.
